publisher: NIST (Center for AI Standards and Innovation)
title: Announcing the AI Agent Standards Initiative for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
key_claim: CAISI launches AI Agent Standards Initiative around three pillars including industry-led agent standards, community-led open-source protocols, and research on agent security and identity infrastructure.
notes: Boundary date — exactly 90 days from scan date; treated as in-window.

publisher: NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE)
title: Accelerating the Adoption of Software and Artificial Intelligence Agent Identity and Authorization (concept paper)
key_claim: NCCoE concept paper proposes a demonstration project applying identity and authorization standards to AI agents in enterprise settings; comments closed 2 April 2026.
notes: Structural anchor — canonical primary source for the identity-and-authorization framing of the signal; just outside soft 3-month window but inside 3-6m band.

title: OIDF responds to NIST on AI agent security (AIIM Threat Modeling Subgroup submission to NIST RFI)
key_claim: OpenID Foundation submitted a formal response to NIST RFI on AI agent security, calling for a 'trust fabric' underneath the technical controls — verifiable credentials, constrained agent authority, and traceable accountability — and pointing to transaction tokens, workload identity federation and authentication extensions for AI tool protocols.
notes: Confirms standards-body convergence around the NIST framing.

title: Research Note: NIST AI Agent Standards — Listening Sessions and Emerging Controls
key_claim: Reports on CAISI's April 2026 sector-specific listening sessions in healthcare, financial services, and education, flagging that sector concerns will likely feed COSAiS overlays and NCCoE practice guides.
notes: Useful for confirming policy-process velocity and bringing in CSA's enterprise practitioner perspective.

title: Business and IT leaders report AI agents are scaling faster than their guardrails (State of AI in the Enterprise 2026)
key_claim: Survey of 3,235 IT/business leaders across 24 countries: only 21% report mature governance for agentic AI; 74% expect at least 'moderate' agent use by 2027; ~80% lack mature agentic governance capabilities including boundary-setting, real-time monitoring, and audit trails.
notes: Quantification anchor — gap between deployment velocity and governance maturity.

title: Why Model Context Protocol is suddenly on every executive agenda
key_claim: MCP has moved from obscure protocol to enterprise governance topic; fewer than 4% of RSA 2026 conference submissions on MCP frame it as opportunity, the rest concentrate on exposure — over-permissioning, prompt injection, tool impersonation, authentication bypass.
notes: Trade-press anchor for the governance-at-protocol-layer framing.

title: Okta announces new blueprint for the secure agentic enterprise (Okta for AI Agents GA 30 April 2026)
key_claim: Okta launches blueprint for secure agentic enterprise built around three questions ('where are my agents, what can they connect to, what can they do?'); cites third-party data that 88% of organizations report suspected or confirmed AI agent security incidents while only 22% treat AI agents as identity-bearing entities.
notes: Vendor source — used as directional corroboration for IAM-vendor pivot, not as anchor for any structural claim.
